cap: Timing explains the two kinds of diabetes in pregnancy. Pregestational diabetes exposes the embryo to high glucose during weeks 3 to 8, so it causes malformations such as caudal regression syndrome, transposition of the great arteries and neural tube defects. Gestational diabetes appears after organogenesis, so it causes overgrowth instead. Screening is done at 24 to 28 weeks, when insulin resistance peaks, with a 50-g challenge and then a 3-hour 100-g test if it is abnormal.
